faceLandmarkLab.title: Camera & Landmark Lab
faceLandmarkLab.description: Before a face can perform as a character, the input has to be trustworthy. This first experiment exposes the local camera, the 478-point face mesh, and the timing of every inference frame.

empty.title: The camera stays off until you start
empty.description: Your browser will ask for permission. Frames are processed locally and are never uploaded.

privacy.title: Local processing only
privacy.description: Video frames and face data stay inside this browser tab. Stopping the experiment releases the camera stream.

headYawLab.title: Head Yaw Lab
headYawLab.description: Turn head orientation from the face transform matrix into a calibrated, inspectable control signal that settles home smoothly.

status.uncalibrated: Face found · calibrate a neutral pose
status.lost: Face lost · easing back to neutral

empty.title: Set a neutral face, then inspect the turn signal
empty.description: Look straight at the camera and calibrate. Video and pose data stay inside this browser.

note.title: From measurement to control signal
note.description: A dead zone quiets neutral jitter, time-based filtering preserves continuity, and face loss never snaps the output to zero.

gazeLab.title: Gaze Lab
gazeLab.description: Measure each iris inside the local frame formed by its eye corners and lids, then adapt binocular fusion when a blink or weak eye makes one side unreliable.

status.searching: Looking for both eyes and irises
status.uncalibrated: Irises tracked · look at center and calibrate
status.low: Eye signal is weak · reducing output weight

empty.title: Look at center, then calibrate both eyes
empty.description: Camera frames and iris data are processed only inside this browser and are never uploaded.

separation.title: Head and gaze separation
separation.description: The upper marker comes from whole-face rotation; the lower marker comes only from each iris relative to its eye contour.

note.title: Coarse gaze estimation, not an eye tracker
note.description: A normal RGB camera is affected by lighting, glasses, occlusion, eye anatomy, and head angle. This signal is useful for character performance, not precision fixation measurement.

faceStateLab.title: Face State Lab
faceStateLab.description: Collapse conditioned head pose, binocular gaze, and expression signals into one reusable, calibrated FaceState so the future 2D performer never needs to understand MediaPipe.

status.searching: Waiting for a complete face signal
status.uncalibrated: FaceState ready · calibrate a neutral state

empty.title: Build a stable contract from raw detection
empty.description: After the camera starts, landmarks, the pose matrix, and blendshapes are converted locally into one FaceState.

boundary.title: Boundary between layers
boundary.description: Only the interpretation layer knows the MediaPipe data format. The next puppet layer consumes FaceState alone.

note.title: Detection can change while the state contract stays stable
note.description: The diagnostic proxy is a direct FaceState visualization. It contains no character styling, spring dynamics, or performance mapping.

puppetLab.title: 2D Puppet Lab
puppetLab.description: Pass the unified FaceState through a deliberately designed performance map to drive an original SVG paper puppet. Different parts respond at different speeds, translating motion into character.

status.searching: Camera online · looking for a face

empty.title: Give three-dimensional input a two-dimensional personality
empty.description: Start the camera to drive this original puppet with head pose, gaze, blinks and mouth expression through layered spring dynamics.

note.title: An original 2D character rendered locally in the browser
note.description: Camera and face data never upload. SVG layers deform in real time, without Live2D models or per-frame image generation.

performerLab.title: 3D Performer Lab
performerLab.description: Extract the local camera once, then build a 3D performance proxy with Face and Hand Landmarker. All 478 face XYZ values, the transform matrix and every blendshape remain intact; semantic states are annotations, not replacements.

status.idle: Performer proxy idle · camera is off
status.searching: Tracking pipeline online · looking for head or hands

empty.title: One camera, two detectors, one shared frame
empty.description: Each camera frame is cloned to isolated Face and Hand workers, then merged into one TrackingFrame. Video and tracking data never upload.

note.title: One observation can branch into different character systems
note.description: The current puppet keeps consuming FaceState. The spatial branch builds PerformerState3D from the same TrackingFrame, ready for a later 3D-to-2D projection lab.

guide.title: How to read a concept card
guide.description: A concept card is not an encyclopedia entry. It is a working snapshot of an idea at its current stage. Sources make it traceable, not automatically authoritative; perspectives, tensions, and a separate sources section remain optional.

flow.ariaLabel: Evidence and perspectives shape the current understanding, which opens into connections, trade-offs, and questions, then changes through revision

understanding.title: Current understanding
understanding.description: The definition and boundaries I am willing to use now, without presenting them as permanent conclusions.

why.title: Why I care
why.description: Why the concept belongs in my research, engineering, product thinking, or worldview.

sources.title: Evidence and sources (optional)
sources.description: Makes facts, definitions, and disagreements traceable; cite close to the relevant claim when possible.

perspectives.title: Perspectives (optional)
perspectives.description: Different roles, scales, or disciplinary lenses through which to view the concept.

connections.title: Connections
connections.description: Places the concept in a knowledge network by relating it to other ideas and practices.

tensions.title: Tensions and trade-offs (optional)
tensions.description: Values or requirements that pull against each other within the concept, not a list of its opposites.

questions.title: Open questions
questions.description: What the current account cannot yet explain and where the note might grow next.

evolution.title: Evolution
evolution.description: When and why the understanding changed, keeping the revision process visible.
